chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the finger, ten dinars of blood money (diyah) if it is severed from its root or paralyzed. He said: And I asked him about the fingers, are they equal in blood money? He said: Yes. He said: And I asked him about the teeth, he said: Their blood money is equal. The meaning in this report is that we interpret it as: if what paralyzes it is done to the finger, it becomes entitled to two-thirds of its blood money, and if it is severed after that, there is one-third of the blood money in it, so it becomes a complete blood money for it, and that does not contradict the detail contained in the first report.

key_terms.الدِّيَة: Blood money or financial compensation for bodily injury

ai.seo_question: What is the blood money (diyah) for a severed or paralyzed finger in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani’s al-Ishtibār clarifies the jurisprudence of *diyah* (blood money) for finger injuries, establishing that severing a finger from its root or causing paralysis incurs two-thirds of the full *diyah*. It further affirms the equality of compensation among fingers and teeth, with the commentator reconciling apparent contradictions by distinguishing between the severity of paralysis versus complete severance, thereby refining the legal application of these penalties.
